# Implementation Plan: Kids Cricket Game Tracker

**Branch**: `001-cricket-game-tracker` | **Date**: 2025-11-07 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-cricket-game-tracker/spec.md`

**Note**: This document was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command following the constitution-defined workflow.

## Summary

Build an offline-first mobile cricket scoring app using Expo/React Native that replaces paper scorebooks for Friday Cricket matches. The app must function flawlessly outdoors in bright sunlight, enforce cricket rules automatically, support multi-device concurrent scoring, and provide instant autosave with optional cloud sync. Core MVP (P1) delivers game setup and real-time scoring; additional priorities add rule enforcement, history/export, crash recovery, and edge case handling.

**Technical Approach**: Leverage Supabase + WatermelonDB for offline-first persistence with optional cloud sync, Yjs CRDT (y-expo-sqlite) for conflict-free multi-device collaboration, and React Context for local state management. UI optimized for outdoor readability with high contrast, large touch targets (≥56px), bold fonts (≥18pt), and strong haptics.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.x with React Native via Expo SDK 54+
**Primary Dependencies**:
- Expo SDK 54+ (React Native runtime, Router, Haptics, Print, Sharing)
- Supabase JS Client v2.46+ (cloud sync, authentication if needed)
- WatermelonDB v0.27+ (offline-first local database)
- Yjs v13.6+ + y-expo-sqlite v1.0+ (CRDT for multi-device sync)
- Custom UI components (outdoor-optimized, high contrast)

**Storage**:
- Local: WatermelonDB (SQLite-based) for game data, players, innings, overs
- Cloud: Supabase (PostgreSQL) for optional synchronization and backup
- Sync: Yjs CRDT layer for conflict-free real-time collaboration

**Testing**:
- Jest + React Native Testing Library (contract and integration tests)
- Detox or Maestro (E2E testing on physical devices)
- Manual outdoor testing (bright sunlight readability validation)

**Target Platform**: iOS 15+ and Android 13+ (smartphones, 5-7 inch screens)

**Project Type**: Mobile (single cross-platform Expo app)

**Performance Goals**:
- Cold start: <2 seconds to home screen
- Scoring tap-to-feedback latency: <100ms
- Autosave: <50ms per scoring event
- UI render: 60fps minimum during active scoring
- Memory: <150MB peak during active game
- Battery: <5% drain per hour of continuous scoring

**Constraints**:
- Must function fully offline (no network dependency for core features)
- Outdoor readability in direct sunlight (high contrast, large fonts, bright mode)
- One-handed operation for primary scoring functions
- Single-level undo only (immutable historical data)
- Player names unique within each team
- Wickets tracked as simple count (no dismissal types)

**Scale/Scope**:
- ~15-20 screens (home, setup wizard, scoring, history, match detail, settings)
- Local storage: 100+ matches (~10-50MB typical usage)
- Concurrent users: 2-5 devices scoring same match simultaneously (via Yjs)
- Codebase: Estimated 8,000-12,000 LOC (TypeScript + JSX)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design.*

### Pre-Phase 0 Evaluation

| Principle | Status | Compliance Notes |
|-----------|--------|------------------|
| **I. Outdoor-First UX** | ✅ PASS | High contrast UI, ≥56px touch targets, ≥18pt fonts, bright mode toggle, strong haptics, one-handed operation all specified in FR-033 through FR-038 |
| **II. Offline-First & Data Reliability** | ✅ PASS | WatermelonDB provides local-first storage, autosave after every event (FR-020), optional cloud sync via Supabase |
| **III. Rule Enforcement Over Flexibility** | ✅ PASS | FR-014 through FR-019 enforce Friday Cricket rules (4 overs/pair, 16 overs/innings, no consecutive bowler, min 1 over/player) |
| **IV. Fast Interaction Over Feature Richness** | ✅ PASS | Single-tap scoring (FR-007 through FR-013), slide-in panels (FR-041), no multi-step flows, single-level undo (FR-013) |
| **V. Test-First Development** | ✅ PASS | Plan includes contract, integration, and snapshot tests; TDD workflow will be enforced during implementation |

**Platform & Technology Constraints**:
- ✅ Expo + React Native + TypeScript (constitution-mandated)
- ✅ Expo Router for file-based navigation (constitution-mandated)
- ✅ React Context for state management (constitution-mandated, no Redux/MobX)
- ✅ WatermelonDB for offline storage (user preference, constitution-compatible)
- ✅ Supabase for optional cloud sync (user preference, constitution-compatible)

**Performance Standards**:
- ✅ Cold start <2s: Achievable with Expo optimizations
- ✅ Tap latency <100ms: React Native can deliver with proper optimization
- ✅ Autosave <50ms: WatermelonDB write performance supports this
- ✅ Memory <150MB: Standard for React Native apps
- ✅ Battery <5%/hour: Achievable with efficient rendering

**Accessibility Requirements**:
- ✅ VoiceOver/TalkBack: Expo provides built-in support
- ✅ Dynamic type: React Native supports system font scaling
- ✅ WCAG AA contrast: High contrast theme meets requirement
- ✅ Haptic feedback: expo-haptics module available

**Result**: All gates PASS. Proceed to Phase 0 research.

### Post-Phase 1 Re-Evaluation

After completing Phase 0 (research.md) and Phase 1 (data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md), re-evaluating all constitutional principles:

| Principle | Status | Post-Implementation Validation |
|-----------|--------|-------------------------------|
| **I. Outdoor-First UX** | ✅ PASS | Research validated high-contrast color palette (#000000 on #FFFFFF), 56px minimum touch targets, 18-48pt fonts, bright mode toggle, haptic feedback strategy using expo-haptics |
| **II. Offline-First & Data Reliability** | ✅ PASS | Data model confirms WatermelonDB provides offline-first with lazy loading, observable queries, <10ms reads, <5ms writes. Supabase sync layer designed for optional cloud backup with last-write-wins for metadata, CRDT for events |
| **III. Rule Enforcement Over Flexibility** | ✅ PASS | Contracts define validation types (BowlingAllocation, BattingPair) with min/max constraints. Rule engine architecture specified in project structure (src/services/ruleEngine.ts) |
| **IV. Fast Interaction Over Feature Richness** | ✅ PASS | Data model optimized for single-tap scoring: OverEvent creation is atomic operation, computed fields avoid complex queries, single-level undo uses soft delete (is_deleted tombstone) |
| **V. Test-First Development** | ✅ PASS | Quickstart.md documents TDD workflow (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR), test pyramid (Contract 50+ → Integration 20-30 → E2E 5-10), Jest + RTL + Detox setup instructions |

**Technology Stack Validation**:
- ✅ TypeScript 5.x: Contracts use strict TypeScript types (Game, Team, Player, Innings, Over, OverEvent interfaces)
- ✅ WatermelonDB: Data model defines complete schemas with indexes, relationships, and performance considerations
- ✅ Yjs CRDT: Sync schema defines YjsGameDocument structure with Y.Array for events, Y.Map for metadata, conflict-free merge strategy
- ✅ Supabase: Quickstart includes SQL schema creation for all tables (games, teams, players, innings, overs, over_events, yjs_documents)
- ✅ Expo SDK 54+: Dependencies listed in quickstart.md (expo-router, expo-haptics, expo-print, expo-sharing)
- ✅ React Context: No Redux/MobX in dependencies, context providers specified in project structure (GameContext, ThemeContext, SyncContext)

**Architecture Validation**:
- ✅ File-based routing: Project structure uses Expo Router (`app/` directory with (tabs) and dynamic routes)
- ✅ Outdoor testing: Quickstart includes manual validation procedures (bright sunlight test, touch target test, one-handed test, haptic test)
- ✅ Performance targets: Research validates all metrics achievable (<2s cold start, <100ms tap latency, <50ms autosave, 60fps, <150MB memory)

**Risk Assessment**:
- ⚠️ **Yjs + WatermelonDB Integration**: Research notes potential complexity (both provide persistence). Mitigation: Use Yjs only for scoring events, WatermelonDB for everything else. Fallback: Defer multi-device sync to v2 if integration too complex.
- ⚠️ **WatermelonDB + Supabase Sync**: Community-maintained sync implementation may have bugs. Mitigation: Custom sync using Supabase REST API. Fallback: Launch without cloud sync, add in v1.1.
- ⚠️ **Outdoor Readability**: Cannot fully validate without physical device testing. Mitigation: Manual test days in direct sunlight. Fallback: Iterate based on user feedback.
- ⚠️ **Low-End Android Performance**: Older devices may struggle with 60fps. Mitigation: Performance testing on low-end devices. Fallback: Detect device tier, disable animations on low-end.

**Result**: All constitutional gates PASS after Phase 1. All technology choices validated as compatible with principles. Risks identified with clear mitigations and fallbacks. Ready to proceed to Phase 2 (tasks.md generation via `/speckit.tasks`).

**Structure Decision**: Using Expo Router file-based structure for mobile app. All UI routes in `app/`, business logic in `src/`, models in `src/models/` (WatermelonDB), sync layer in `src/sync/` (Yjs + Supabase). Tests organized by type (contract, integration, e2e) following constitution testing tiers.

## Complexity Tracking

> No constitution violations detected. All requirements align with constitutional principles.

**Justifications for Technology Choices** (not violations, but rationale):

| Choice | Rationale | Constitution Alignment |

| Supabase + WatermelonDB | User preference for offline-first with optional cloud sync; aligns with Principle II (Offline-First & Data Reliability) | ✅ Constitution allows "SQLite/MMKV" and user chose WatermelonDB (SQLite-based) |
| Yjs CRDT (y-expo-sqlite) | User preference for multi-device concurrent scoring; enables conflict-free collaboration without complex UI | ✅ Not mandated but compatible; supports FR-025 requirement |
| React Context (not Redux) | Constitution explicitly requires React Context, rejecting Redux/MobX complexity | ✅ Constitution-mandated (Mobile-Specific Constraints) |
| Expo Router | Constitution specifies Expo Router for file-based navigation | ✅ Constitution-mandated (Mobile-Specific Constraints) |

No simpler alternatives rejected; all choices align with or are mandated by constitution.
